utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al., thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today is the 28th of October, 2008. Good morning to the accused, the Defence counsel. Good morning to you, Mr. Scott and to your associate, and good morning to all the people helping us. Good morning, Witness. Mr. Registrar, you have an IC number, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you. Prlic Defence has submitted objection to the OTP list of documents tendered through Witness Simunovic Marinko which was previously given Exhibit number IC 00872. The objection list submitted by 1D shall be given Exhibit number IC 00875. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Again good morning, Mr. Karnavas. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. President, Your Honours, everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before I begin, Your Honour, just to let you know, we have provided you hard copies of 1D 00828. Yesterday the Bench was interested in Article 38, and again we provided 1D 00897, Article 66 was of interest, so we provide the hard copies in the eventuality you wish to look at them and ask questions later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's pick up where we left off, Mr. Tomic. Let's look at 1D 00031. We're still dealing with the issues of taxation. You'll see that this is a decree on the level of interest to be applied to the amounts of taxes, contributions, stamp, duty, and so on. Could you please tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about a decision which defines the obligation to pay interest in the case of belated payments of public revenue. This is meant for the protection of the monies due to the inflation at the time. The latest decision at republic level was 8 per cent from March till August, and then we continued to set monthly penal interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Next document is 1D 00034. This is the decree on the implementation of the law on customs and customs tariffs, and we can see it's rather comprehensive. If you could please provide us a brief explanation.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a customs tariff which was taken over from the ex-Yugoslav customs tariff. That was based on a decision made by republic. It was published in the Official Gazette and became available to all who needed the services of the customs administration. The customs tariff is 1 to 2 points below that in Croatia. The intention was to create a financial interest for the import of goods into the area of HZ HB instead of buying goods in Croatia and a tax being paid in Croatia too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00041. This is a decision on the application of currency rates, and if you could provide us with a commentary on this, in particular with respect to Articles 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision defines the manner of converting foreign currency into the currency use by HZ HB. There was no communication with the central bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and thus there was no official list of exchange rates. In the area of HZ HB there was no bank with its head office there, so they wouldn't set exchange rates either. So this was a decision to apply the list of exchange rates of the Privredna Banka Zagreb, a commercial bank which was one of the co-founders of the Hrvatska Banka Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, P 00447, dated 22 September 1992. This is a decree on the regulation of payment transactions in Croatian dinars, and if you could please provide us with an explanation on this.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation on the ground was the following: The Croatian dinar was already means of payment in all municipalities of HZ HB, and this decree defines how the payment system in the area of HZ HB is to be conducted -- or, rather, is to take place. All accounts with the SDK are in BiH dinars, and this decree stipulates that subordinate accounts shall be set up in Croatian dinars. So that technically if the account number was 11800630128, the account number in Croatian dinars would be 118006301000128. It was a subordinate account of the main account opened in BiH dinars. Later, subordinate accounts in German marks were opened, too, and the initial -- initial figure would be 2. Accounts in dollars would start with 3, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, why was it necessary to pass a decree regulating the payment transactions in Croatian dinars? Was this some sort of attempt to Croatise the area by way of introducing the Croatian dinar?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title of the decree is "Decree on the regulation ... " The Croatian dinar was already present. Due to the situation it found its way into the area of HZ HB. Now the question was how we can control the money to avoid cash payment, because if payment is effected through the SDK it is easier to levy taxes and contributions which is one of the main tasks. So this has nothing to do with a rapprochement with Croatia, because the same was later done with the German mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, maybe I failed to ask this question yesterday, but wasn't there any way to impose the Bosnian dinar on everyone? In other words, use that as the only means of transactions, monetary transactions, and disallow the usage of any other currency such as the Deutschmark, the Croatian dinar, the US dollar, the French franc?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first there were such attempts, but as I said yesterday, there was no demand for BiH dinars on the part of the companies that operated at the time, because they couldn't do anything with those dinars in Croatia or anywhere. They -- they couldn't convert them into other currencies because in Croatia the BiH dinar was not on the list of exchange rates, and the same applies to other countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00038. This is a decree on the organisation and functioning of the Public Accounting Service, and this is 29 September 1992. If you could comment on this, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree sets forth the organisation and functioning of the Public Accounting Service, and it says here that it shall be organised and function in accordance with the provision of the law on the SDK of the Republic of BiH so that the organisation of the SDK in HZ HB was the same as that in Republic of BiH, only in a limited area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Next I'm going to go through a series of documents that are interconnected. I'll read them off first and then we'll go through them one by one, but I'll read them off for everyone's convenience. We're going to start off with 1D 01678, then we'll go to 1D 01350, 1D 02127, 1D 02128, and then finally P 01063. So if we could look at the first one, 1D 01678. Could you please tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the agreement with the government commissioner about one truck with BiH dinars remaining in HZ HB, that truck stayed or was left in Siroki Brijeg and Posusje, and in the offices of the SDK at Siroki Brijeg and Posusje that money was stored. This is a report or protocol on the acceptance of that money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this -- in the document we see your name, but we also see Mr. Mate Erkapic. Could you please tell us who he was or is?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the government commissioner. I mean the government of BiH from Sarajevo. And it was his duty to transport the BiH dinars that were printed in Celje, Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday during your narrative you did indicate that that money could be used and in fact was used, I believe in Central Bosnia. So let's look at some of these other documents. 1D 01350. Could you please tell us what -- what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report of the SDK, and it was sent to the finance department. This shows under which orders which quantity of BiH dinars were issued. We're talking about a total of 13 orders, and the total value of the BiH dinar as delivered is stated here also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We go on to the next document 1D 02127. 1D 02127. And here's -- this is a decision on the method of granting monetary assistance to the municipal Croatian Defence Councils in Central Bosnia, and if you could comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO HZ HB at its meeting on November the 27th, 1992, decided that this quantity of BiH dinars is -- shall be given to the HVOs in Central Bosnia which were areas where the BiH dinar was in circulation, and that money shall be used for the provision of commodities and for other needs of the HVOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And we can see from Article I where it talks about the monetary assistance granted in BH dinars; right? That's in Article I.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's about on to 1D 02128, 1D 02128. This is a conclusion. If you could please comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the allocation of that money in -- a person with individual protocol signed with each municipal HVO, a report was drafted on the allocation of that money, and based on that the HVO HZ HB adopted this conclusion about the distribution of BiH dinars and the assistance granted to municipal HVOs in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And then finally if we go to P 01063.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we're going to focus on page 8, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Please tell us what -- what is this document about, and if you could give us -- provide us with a comment on page 8.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the meeting where the conclusion was adopted about the allocation of dinars to Central Bosnia, and based on that, the conclusion was drafted and signed as we saw on -- in document 1D 02128.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The conclusion's on page 4 in your document, page 8 in the English document. Do you see it on page 4 of the B/C/S where it makes reference to Zenica, Vitez, Travnik, Novi Travnik, Usora --

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And finally along with this package, I should have also noted is 1D 02222, 2222. This is from 29 April 1993. This is an article in Slobodna Dalmacija and subject introduction of BH dinar. It's an article apparently authored by Dr. Jadranko Prlic. Are you familiar with this article and if, so, can you please comment?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with it. This article was triggered by the successless attempt to introduce the dinar as the currency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because in a very short time the exchange rate dropped drastically, and it was mostly used for transactions in the black market, if I may say that. And the exchange rate itself differed from island to island, as it were, whether we're talking about Tuzla or some other territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Due to our allocation of aid to the Croatian municipalities in Central Bosnia, and in late September the exchange rate was about 5.000 dinars to a Deutschmark, and in December when the last shipment was made, the last shipment of BH dinars to municipal HVOs in Central Bosnia, the exchange rate was from 8.000 to even 10.000 BH dinars to a Deutschmark. And this is an article written by Dr. Prlic. He wrote it as an expert, and it's about confidence in currency. A currency should be able to make people safe and avoid -- prevent them to -- to be afraid for their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One last question concerning this article, concerning Dr. Prlic's observations. Do you agree or disagree with them, and do they accurately reflect the situation as it existed at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless there are any questions from the bench, I'll -- concerning this discrete issue, I'll move on, Your Honours. I see there are no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have a question. Witness, earlier on we saw a series of documents showing that BiH dinars that had been printed in Slovenia had been dispatched to municipal HVOs in Zenica, Vares, and so forth. The amounts in BiH dinars that would get to the Vares HVO, for instance, what would happen to that money? What would become of it? Would that stay in safes? Was it distributed? What happened to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVOs in the municipalities in Central Bosnia bought commodities. For example, coal, coal for heating in Travnik. They could pay for that coal in BiH dinars. In Zenica they could buy iron, construction iron for BH dinars. So the HVOs were turning that money into commodities immediately, or they would pay the liabilities already incurred and thus they would protect themselves against inflation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand properly, initially the HVO did not oppose the BiH dinar to be circulated since the BH dinar was used for the purchase of commodities. You give the example for Travnik, but you might be able to give other examples. Correct me if I'm wrong, but my impression is that based on the documents and based on your statement, my impression is that the HVO used the BH dinar and was not against it being used. Is this a possible conclusion one can draw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. There is no one decision of the HVO HZ HB that bans the use of BiH dinars for -- as a means of payment. This has exclusively to do with the market at the time and the demand for BH dinars on the one hand, and on the other hand it has to do with the protection of public revenue and property, because the inflation of the BiH dinar was too great, and also the quantity of the money was limited. We later also had such problems with the Croatian dinar. That's why subsequently the German mark was introduced into the payment system, because in the area there simply was not enough cash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I read again what you have just said about in -- oh, the inflation, if I link that to the article written by Dr. Prlic that was published on the 29th of April, 1993, that is several months later, in that article Dr. Prlic speaks about the inflation, and towards the end of the article Dr. Prlic seems to indicate that as far as he can assess the situation, the best solution to combat this excessive inflation would be to have an agreement between the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia in order, as it were, to regulate interstate regulations. Is this the solutions -- the solution he advocates in order to solve the problems that arise because of the war and the events, that is, an agreement between the two republics, possibly to restore confidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the conclusion of this article there is an explanation about the creation of the fiscal and financial system in Herceg-Bosna, and there is this claim that it is the best of all the bad solutions, because given the circumstances, given the chaos, the fact that the state was not functioning, the institutions were not functioning, there are no good solutions. All solutions are bad. All solutions are makeshift solutions, but here it says that this solution, in line with the legal system in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the legal system in the Republic of Croatia insofar as it pertains to the use of the Croatian dinar. In other words, we did not use the Croatian dinar in contravention of the Croatian laws. We could not issue money. We did not participate in the monetary policy. We did not influence it in any way. We used the Croatian dinar in the same way in which citizens of Slovenia or any other state where Croatian dinar existed on the exchange rate lists could use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. You seem to be well-versed in your subject, a specialist as it were, as was Mr. Prlic. These are rather technical and complex issues. In light of inflation, in light of the fact that three currencies were used, the Deutschmark, the Croatian dinar, and BH dinar, at any time did you contemplate contacting the IMF, the World Bank, the large international organisations that are competent in such matters? But since it was a state of war, were you not able to get that kind of support or find such a solution and turn to these institutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In formal terms Bosnia and Herzegovina was not a member of the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, the EBRD, or the European Bank. States are members of those institutions, and we did not have any contacts, and we did not pursue any activities in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have seen some documents and other witnesses have mentioned this already. Did the EU not take an interest in what was happening in Bosnia-Herzegovina and was not interested in your field of endeavour? Had studies not been carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no contacts with the representatives of the European Union in this sphere. They mostly focused on humanitarian work and military aspects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your answers. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the World Bank or the IMF sent representatives at that time, we're talking 1992, 1993, to Bosnia-Herzegovina to provide any technical assistance or any assistance that they might have been able to provide?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that at that time Bosnia and Herzegovina was not a member of the World Bank and of the International Monetary Fund. This issue was regulated only after the Washington agreements were signed. The first contacts with the World Bank were established after the Washington Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when the World Bank eventually did come to BiH after the Washington Agreement, were you involved in any way with their activities?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, as the Minister of Finance, I together with the governor of the central bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina led a mission to Warsaw, Poland, and this mission initiated talks about the establishing of the financial system in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you say Minister of Finance, you're talking about being the Minister of Finance for Bosnia-Herzegovina while at the same time you were the minister of finance for the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was my title after the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on now to 1D 00032. This is a decree on the conditions for organising an insurance organisations during the state of war. If you could please look at this and give us a brief commentary. We note in Article 1, for instance, references to republican laws. Could you please give us a brief explanation?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this decree regulates the -- the issue of organising the organisations in the sphere of insurance in the area of the HZ HB. The republican laws are adopted, and those laws in turn adopted the laws of the former Yugoslavia, because no new laws had been passed at the republican level. And since, as I've already indicated, in the area of the HZ HB they were for the most part just the branch offices of those insurance companies. This makes it possible for those branch offices to establish legal entities in the area of the HZ HB and thus to continue operating and providing services in the field of insurance. And as far as the insurance companies from countries not in Bosnia and Herzegovina, they had to establish new legal entities in Bosnia and Herzegovina in HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I believe that was part of your narrative yesterday with respect to the green card, and now we see the actual legal instrument related to this -- this matter; right? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. 1D 00035. This is a decree on the terms under which legal and natural persons with headquarters outside the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina may conduct business in HZ HB territory. Could you please explain this -- this document for us.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said a number of times. Banks had their branches there, and the branches continued to operate as part of those companies that had seats in Croatia, Slovenia, or any other state, in fact. Of course this created great problems from the point of view of the payment of taxes and contributions, and we simply passed this decree that by the 31st of October they had to, if they wanted to continue to operate in the area of HZ HB in Bosnia and Herzegovina that they had to register as legal entities. In other words, they had to have their management there and they had to have their account opened with the SDK, and that was one of the reasons -- the principal account. That was one of the reasons why banks did found banks in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The insurance companies founded the insurance companies in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and other companies followed suit and founded their daughter companies in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they were then compelled to pay taxes and contributions in HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00051. This is a decree on individual business activity during the imminent threat of war. Just a very brief comment looking at Article 2 in particular.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree adopts all the regulations enforced in Bosnia and Herzegovina about small enterprises, cafes, restaurants, butcher shops, transport companies, hauliers, because this was regulated by a special law, and this decree in fact adopts the republican regulations and they apply in the area of HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this document on the screen talks about those companies set up during the state of war, I would like to thank Mr. Karnavas for having shown us document ID 00897 and Article 66. When I read Article 66 of this document, I realise the following: I would like you to comment this for me since you were a major player in the implementation of Article 66. First of all, this law is a law that goes back to the 1980s since this bill had been adopted in the time of the former Yugoslavia. As far as I see, this general popular defence goes back to the 9th of February, 1984. This text must have been adopted in the event of an attack against Yugoslavia, perhaps by X, Y, or Z, but this text in Article 66 states that during a wartime or during a state of imminent war, the -- the Assembly is responsible for the municipality and may act. On looking at this Article 66, I'm wondering whether in Mostar the following was acknowledged: President Izetbegovic made a statement and declared that it was an imminent state of war. The municipality then, on the basis of this text, decided to take on some areas. For instance, if we look at Articles -- the last Articles, 308 -- 389, for instance, the municipal laws are there to finance the purchase of weapons. Now, when these texts were adopted pursuant to Article 66, was this because everybody felt that since there was a state of war, imminent threat of war, that the municipalities had full powers as had been enshrined in the law adopted in 1984?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This article, Article 66, envisaged the establishment of the Presidency of the municipality, and it's taking over from the Assembly that could not be in session at the time. The Presidency could take decisions in the sphere of the defence that had to do at the municipal levels, because they were republican laws that stipulated what the republican TO should do, and this was financed from the budget of the republic, the organisation of the republican Territorial Defence. And here the municipal -- the municipality has to finance the needs in its area, and it passes decisions related to the mobilisation, the procurement of whatever is needed for the civilian protection, for the preparation of the reserve forces, because if you look at Article 389, in paragraph 3 it says preparations of the reserve militia except for the needs financed by the republic. So the republic had its own jurisdiction and the municipality had its own jurisdiction, but at the beginning of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina because the republic [as interpreted] did not perform its job, the municipalities took upon themselves to perform both the tasks that were in their jurisdiction and also those tasks that under the jurisdiction of the republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, what the municipalities were doing, well, they were doing this in line with the law passed in 1984.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Partly in accordance with the law. Under the law they had certain powers but they also assumed the powers of the republic because the republic did not perform those tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe on line 15 of the previous -- of page 16 it should say republic and not municipality where he says "because the municipality did not perform its job," it should say "because the republic did not perform its job." That can be checked later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00052. This is a decree on placing in abeyance the process of transformation of social capital, and yesterday, for instance, we did see one document, I believe it was Apro Holding, where you did comment a little bit on the privatisation process, as it were, that had -- had been started by I think it was Markovic, but can you comment on this particular decree? What does it set out to do? This is 14 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was passed to protect property. At the time it was still socially owned property which was in the process of being privatised to protect it against wild privatisation, out of control privatisation. There was not any institution at the republican level to monitor the process of privatisation. Once the war broke out this institution no longer functioned. The payment of salaries, that was the way in which the workers were able to purchase shares in their companies. The salaries were not paid out regularly in most companies. And the third thing was to protect the property against speculators, against those who wanted to buy shares and not actually pay what they were worth in an illegal manner. And this whole process was placed in abeyance, it was suspended, and the companies could continue operating in accordance with the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. 1D 00039. This is compensation of war damages sustained in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. If you could give us a brief explanation and of course please look at Article 1 because we see the date 20 October 1991 as the commencing date.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the HZ HB, there were companies that wanted to resume operation, and they had sustained a lot of damage to their property, buildings, facilities, equipment, and they wanted to be given some privileges in order to be able to restore and reconstruct this property. The same went for private property, houses, vehicles, things of that sort. The municipalities each issued their own decisions regulating this, but this disrupted the financial system because they exempted companies from paying taxes, contributions, and so on. This decree tried to regulate this issue for the whole area of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to establish single methodology, commissions, the way in which they were to operate. There is an addendum to this decree which defines the manner in which damage is to be determined for each kind of facility and building. The date, the 29th of September, 1992, it was -- or, rather, the 20th of October, 1991, interpreter's correction, this had to do with the arrival of the reservists to Mostar because this was the date when the damage began to be inflicted because the tanks caused destruction in the street. They destroyed some lamp posts, things of that sort, and then it proceeded from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next document, 1D 00048. This is a decree on the implementation of the law on stamp duties. Could you just give us a very brief commentary on this. It's rather comprehensive, but perhaps you can comment. We can see from the very first article that it makes reference to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here this is again the adoption of the republican law on stamp duty, and its published in an Official Gazette so that it could apply. The difference between this regulation and the republican regulation is that the stamp duty is denominated of Croatian dinars and the organs of the HZ HB are not treated as state organs, because in the republican regulations there is always mention of state organs and this is yet another indication of the fact that this is just a provisional decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00049. This is a decree on the budget of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. If you could please comment on this. And it might be of interest also at this point in time because we see this quite often in other decrees, Article 2 says: "All provisions of the Law on Financing Budgetary Expenditures in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina which are not contrary to the provisions of this decree shall be applied." We see similar language with other decrease and perhaps you could comment why was it necessary to include this language which is not contrary to provisions of this decree? Why was it necessary to have that language?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the communications breakdown and because there was no flow of information about legislative activity at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Those laws, because of the situation in the field and the general circumstances, had to be adapted in some ways, and this is why, for instance, the introduction of the Croatian dinar as the currency in which the budget is denominated, in the process regulating the budget of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it is denominated in BH dinars, but we used the Croatian dinars although -- because we had decided to regulate the payment transaction -- transactions in this manner, and we decided to denominate the budget in the Croatian dinars because the Croatian dinars were the prevalent currency in this area. This decree is important because it was an attempt to lay foundation for the adoption of the first budget, because the funds that came in were used pursuant to individual decisions of the HVO HZ HB, but in line with the practice it was necessary to have a budget, but the budget has the revenues and the expenditures. In the initial stage the budgetary revenues could not meet the expenditure side, so technically the budget was in a deficit because we could not cover the budgetary deficit by getting loans or with the primary issue from the central bank because it was not -- it was simply not possible to do that. And that is why the budget as a document that should balance the revenues and expenditures was not adopted in 1992. This was an attempt to lay foundations for the budget in 1993, but again in 1993 it was not adopted as a document. The first budget was adopted pursuant to this decree in 1994, not before that, and that is why Article 5 reads that each department of the Croatian Defence Council of the HZ HB should state their needs for every three months. It is usually done annually. And the draft budget should be made by the finance department based on the materials put forward by the departments, other departments, and then the HVO HZ HB should go through it, consolidate a draft which would then be put before the Presidency of the HVO HZ HB for its adoption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00130. This is a decree on establishing the Chamber of Commerce. It says Chamber of economy, but as I understand it we're talking about the Chamber of Commerce. And if you could explain to us what the chamber of Commerce did, how it functioned, just very, very briefly and of course perhaps give us an explanation of why we see Mate Boban's name at the end of this particular decree.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chamber of the Economy before the war was a para-state institution. It was founded pursuant to a state law, and all economic operators had to be its members and pay membership dues. At the same time, the state transferred some public powers on the Chamber so that the Chamber dealt with some issues on behalf of a public body acting like a public body, such as setting the number of workers to be sent abroad. The former Yugoslavia would get a certain quota, say a hundred thousand workers per year, who were allowed to go to Germany to work, and the chamber would then identify the needs or the interest of individual companies and then make a list of priority and make -- make allotments -- make allotment. So the state had to establish a chamber for that system to continue operating. Before the war, in the area of HZ HB, there was a regional chamber in Mostar, and the people from that chamber had drafted this decree which was adopted, and the chamber was to continue functioning along -- in accordance with the regulations that were in force in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go to 1D 00122, just very briefly. We see these are the rules on the pass of a special emblem -- I mean 112. 1D 00112. Rules on the pass and special emblem of authorised officials, and if you could focus primarily on Article 3 but very briefly tell us what it is about.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the identification of officers of the customs administration of HZ HB we had to issue them IDs and badges, and this defines the content of that ID card, just like memorandums and decisions had in the letterhead the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then HZ HB, et cetera. So the same applied to official documents of the customs administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you to slow down just a little bit to make sure that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to slow down so that the interpreters can keep up with you. If we go on to 1D 00106. Yesterday we talked a little bit about the SDK. You told us how it functioned. You also told us how at one point it wasn't functioning. If you could look at this document, 1D 00106. Please tell us about this decision.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is decision on the appointment of the management of the SDK. Mate Erkapic was appointed, who before the war was director of the principal branch office, which was in Sarajevo before the war, and his deputy is Jusuf Skoljic, who was a director of the principal branch office in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to ask you to please slow down a little bit, because -- while you know the area, some of us do not. Now, Erkapic worked at the -- in Sarajevo, so did he have any specific knowledge in order to get -- in order for him to be appointed to this particular position?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that he was the director of the central unit of the SDK of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and its remit went as far as the main branch offices. So he had the greatest knowledge of all persons available. And Mr. Skoljic was the director of the branch office of Mostar, which is the next lower level, and Mr. Skoljic was appointed deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And the deputy, was he a Croat or was he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The deputy was a Muslim, and the director was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. P 00735. This is a decision on the import of goods from the Republic of Croatia. If you could please give us a quick explanation. Why was this decision necessary, and what does this decision attempt to -- to do?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time activities are in progress to establish border crossings and attempt to make possible the import of goods into the area of HZ HB or, at the time, Bosnia-Herzegovina. There were dozens of crossings, of course, between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, roads and footpaths, because previously there had been no border. Goods came in from Croatia without obstacles, and taxes were paid in Croatia. As I said, it was our goal to have as many goods imported in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the HZ HB, and to levy taxes there, but so -- but we found out that if we implement the existing laws and regulations there would be a price difference between goods produced in Croatia and imported into the area of HZ HB and that difference would exceed 20 per cent. If you remember those customs tariffs, 7 per cent plus 7.5 per cent plus 1 per cent, and if we add to that the rate, the applicable rate from the tariff, the total is a difference of at least 20 per cent. So what was happening, people were going to Croatia, they would buy goods there, and without any control they imported those goods into the area of HZ HB. We could not control that. We had no data, and taxes were not levied for the budget of HZ HB. That's why this decree was passed under which for goods from Croatia only a -- only a small amount was paid for the process of clearing customs, and thus we wanted to achieve that people stop going to Croatia and pay for fuel, et cetera, because we wanted to make it more attractive for them to buy goods in the area of HZ HB. Article 4 reads that goods that transit the area of HZ HB and go on to, say, Zenica or Tuzla, that no customs duties would be levied on them although they are goods from Croatia. They will only be registered by customs, and the drivers of the vehicles would be given accompanying documents which they would submit at their final destination as is stipulated by the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you mentioned that there was no border before. What do you mean by that? I mean, just so the Judges understand what is happening for the first time in this area.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout history there was no physical border that you could make out on the ground. The border wasn't marked. There were no ramps or no structures. So this was a border that actually ran through people's houses, because people had their houses on one side of the border and their fields on the other. It was very common. Likewise, it was very difficult to identify the borderline, so that overnight the ramps would be moved a hundred or 200 metres to one or the other side because the locals would say, "No, no. This isn't where the border is. It's over there," et cetera. We didn't have detailed maps based on exact surveys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at 1D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please, before we move to this document. This issue of the border, as to this issue, if I understand properly, during the former Yugoslavia you did not have any internal borders as they are currently understood. For instance, a border between Switzerland and Germany, do you mean to say that there was no such border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an administrative border, so it was known which plots of land were in Bosnia-Herzegovina or in Croatia. So it was clear in the cadaster, but there were no markings on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand properly, it was you at the level of Herzegovina who set up a border between Herzegovina and Croatia by putting check-points or -- or border posts and customs control in order to fight the import of goods which would distort or have economic or financial negative consequences in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So you were the ones who created the border.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. Initially we had check-points, but when the customs service arrived there, ramps were set up which were controlled by civilian and military police, and on the other side Croatia set up their own ramps and structures with police and customs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when crossing borders, everybody here in this courtroom must have crossed a border at some point in their lives. Sometimes you have flags, you have uniforms, and you have people who man the borders. On the side of Herzegovina, what kind of flags would you find?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the emblems had been defined, the flag was the flag of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there anywhere any mention of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The authorised persons at those border crossings, that is to say customs officers and police officers, had ID cards that read Republic of Herzegovina HZ HB customs or police or whichever service they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were stamps created for trucks transporting goods? Would their papers be stamped, their manifestos, their customs papers, would they be stamped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The stamp of the customs administration of HZ HB was applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you find the words "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina" on those stamps? Maybe I go too much into detail, but if I raise the issue it's because it's important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same -- the stamp looked just the same as all other stamps used in HZ HB. I can't remember exactly, but I know that all memorandums also read Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but I'm not sure now about the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, just to get things clear, do you know whether an analogous border existed between Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Muslim part of it, and probably Croatia and maybe other states?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No such border was in existence, because the area controlled by the army of BiH was in direct contact with the Croatian border. The nearest such area was the area around Bihac, but then on the other side of the border there was the area of the Serbian Krajina in the Republic of Croatia, and a border -- border authorities were for the first time established there after the Storm operation in Croatia. That's the border crossing of Izacic. That was the first border crossing manned by the staff of the then border service of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas. Before we start, just a clarification for the record, if I might suggest, and if I'm wrong then I'll certainly be told so, but the witness said at line -- on page 27, line 10, "No such border was in existence because the area controlled by the army of BiH was in direct contact with the Croatian border." I suppose he meant to say that it was not in contact with the Croatian border. If that could be clarified, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no area controlled by the army of BiH which bordered on the Republic of Croatia except for that part of Croatia which was then under the control of the Serbian Krajina, and the customs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had check-points and would levy customs on goods at check-points --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat? We didn't get the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer. Please repeat the last part of your answer so -- because the interpreters have not understood it.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the customs administration of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had the first contact with the documentation about goods entering Bosnia-Herzegovina or would receive such documentation from check-points in areas under the control of the HVO or the BiH army -- and the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as there is an interruption now, it may be good to clarify a possible error. Page 26, line 16 and 17. You asked the witness whether the authorised persons at border crossings, that is customs officers or police officers -- sorry, that is actually the answer. You asked whether anywhere on the border there was explicit mention of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The witness replied that the authorised persons on the border, that is customs officers and police officers, wore badges which read "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina HZ HB customs or police," et cetera, but the transcript reads that they have ID cards. Your question obviously referred to the symbols, what was -- what anybody would be able to see, but ID cards are not clearly visible. They are mostly carried in pockets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is extremely relevant. Could you clarify this point, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. The badge and the official ID were two parts of a whole. The -- the ID card was under the badge, and it read "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina HZ HB," the way it is described in the document that we saw a short while ago. It was document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 112, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: In order to get the full picture about borders, was there or was there not a border between the HZ HB and the rest of BiH, Bosnia and Herzegovina? Was there a border? Was there no border? Was there something between a border and no border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were check-points, and at those check-points there were no staff of the customs administration of HZ HB, because to us in practice, in the implementation and in the documents, these check-points were never treated as border crossings. So goods coming from Zenica, for example, such as the construction iron bought in Zenica or iron bought from Grude, it was transported without levying customs duties. It was treated as internal transport within Bosnia-Herzegovina. Unfortunately, it didn't work the same way in the opposite direction. The customs administration of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina would levy customs duties on goods that were accompanied with invoices issued in Grude or other places in HZ HB. So those goods were treated the same way as goods coming from Croatia, Slovenia, or any other country. And in this part about the import of goods from Croatia, in Article 4 you can see that goods transiting the area of HZ HB, that is goods travelling to areas controlled by the army of BiH, are -- on such goods no customs duties were levied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I think that it's time for a break. We're going to have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall first give the floor to our registrar, because we need an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution has submitted an objection to Prlic Defence list of documents tendered through Witness Simunovic Marinko, which was previously given Exhibit number IC 00870. The objection list submitted by the OTP shall be given Exhibit number IC 00876. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor. I would like to advise you of the fact that you have had so far four hours and 41 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I should advise the Bench that it may be necessary to go beyond the six hours that I had anticipated. Of course it will be taken out of our overall scope of time, and as you've indicated to the witness yesterday that there's a high probability that we will go into next week. There is no witness scheduled for next week precisely because of that reason, but I do think that this is a very important witness and a complicated subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Picking up where we left off at 1D 00108, we see this is a decision on the border crossings with the Republic of Croatia, and this is dated 12 November 1992, and we can see in Article 2 the various locations. Can you confirm that the border crossings are between the republic of -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia, all of these border crossings?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the border crossings in the area of Herzegovina, between Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and those border crossings are in fact still in existence today, and they're used for crossing of goods and passengers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next document, 1D 00114, and we'll discuss this rather in detail. This is a decree on organising and operation of the financial police, and I'm going to ask you a series of questions. We'll go step-by-step. This is dated 12 -- 2 December 1992. First and foremost, could you please tell us what the financial police was, whether it existed prior to this decree in Bosnia-Herzegovina, this institution?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This institution did not exist before. It is part of the transition. After the Washington Agreement the financial police was set up in Bosnia and Herzegovina too. Why was financial police established at that time? For two reasons. First of all, the republican public revenue department, an organ that controlled the work of the municipal public revenue departments, did not function. There were republican inspectors who came from Sarajevo to municipalities to control how the municipal public revenue departments, for instance, I was a director of one of those before the war, how we collect taxes to be paid into the budget of the republic, of the SIZ, and so on. But this no longer existed. Municipal public revenue departments were still there, and under the laws they still had the duty to collect taxes at the municipal level, but they did not have any kind -- any way to exercise control above the municipal level. The second reason was that the SDK also did not function at its full capacity, and its inspectors did not function. And for this reason and the situation in the field was such that the municipalities issued their own regulations the way they saw fit and then violated the regulations that we passed in order to make sure that they have as much money as possible for their own municipality. They amended our regulations, in fact. And this decree sets up a special institution called the financial police that in effect replaced the republican inspectors from the republican public revenue department and the inspectors of the SDK that existed before the war. The fundamental task was to control the implementation of the HZ HB regulations at the level of the HZ HB in municipalities, public enterprises and other entities that were duty-bound to implement those regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again I'll ask you to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll ask you to go a little slower. Now, you indicated that after the Washington Agreement, financial police were instituted throughout the federation, and as I understand it today, it's throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It remained a federal institution, because Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the next step of the transition, adopted the VAT and an administration for indirect taxation was established, and at the level of the state it actually controlled the implementation of the laws covering that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But the federation, when it adopted or when it implemented a financial police, was it based on a new methodology, new functions, new responsibilities, or was it based essentially on what was initiated by the HVO HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first law on financial police of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina practically copied the text of this decree. The principles, the contents, the powers were all copied from this decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we just go through this very quickly. Article 5 sets out essentially what are the duties and functions of the financial police; correct? Inspect, monitor, supervise, check, prepare, undertake, carry out.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at Article 8, it would appear that the financial police answer to your particular department, the HVO HZ HB financial department. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Under Article 11 we see the requirements for somebody holding the post or various posts within the financial police. And then we see in Article 14 that the appointments and dismissals are actually published in the Official Gazette. I take it through Article 14 there's -- it provides for transparency, does it not?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just very quickly, if we look at Article 23, which may be of assistance for other purposes, Article 23 reads: "At the proposal of the head of the finance department the HVO HZ HB shall adopt a separate set of rules," and it goes on. If you could explain to us what is meant by proposal by the head of the finance department?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that the finance department drafts some rules or other regulations about uniforms, arms, and so on, and then that the head of the department would submit this document to the HVO HZ HB so that it could be put on the agenda. And then at its session the HVO HZ HB has a discussion about the document and adopts it. Once it is adopted it is signed by the authorised official. If the HVO HZ HB can adopt it, then the president of the HVO HZ HB signs it and after that this regulation is published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, is a proposal automatically adopted? In other words, are there proposals which are rejected or modified?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were proposals that had to be modified or returned to the author for corrections because of some other elements that were important, some information, input that was provided by other departments. For instance, if in our decree or a decision we stipulated that the misdemeanour court would have jurisdiction over violations and then the justice department indicates that it is not the misdemeanour court but some higher court, then we had to amend the decision, and then after that the decision would be adopted and published.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether proposals that were presented before the HVO HZ HB were rejected? Can we assume that once -- if it says "proposal," automatically it would be adopted -- it would have been adopted at some point?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The departments submitted documents and then there was the debates at the session, and if there was a number of objections or amendments, they would return to the author for modification, and then they would be again subject of a discussion at the next session and then finally they were adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If we look at Article 24, if you could just comment very briefly, because it talks about: "In performing the duties within their remit and under the circumstances specified by the Law on Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic, financial police inspectors may bring in citizens into a competent organ." What is this referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the municipal public revenue departments were under the jurisdiction of the municipal HVO, HVOs, and they were in charge of the implementation of the financial segments of the regulations, but because of the needs of the municipal budgets and because of the pressure exerted by the presidents of the municipal HVOs, they often violated those provisions and implemented the municipal regulations in order to ensure extra revenue. But when we wanted to hold them responsible for that, the fact is that they were appointed by the municipal HVO presidents and they were at the same time members of the HVO Presidency and we were supposed to report to them. We were responsible to them. So it was a weird situation where for all intents and purposes our hands were tied. We could not really implement the -- we could not enforce the legislation. And the purpose of this institution was to be an independent institution set up at the level of the HZ HB who could then enforce the regulations. The problem was in the field, because there were a lot of efforts to obstruct the work of the inspectors. Sometimes the companies would summon members of the units to intimidate the inspectors of the financial police to prevent them from carrying out the inspection. Those units received donations from those companies. This decree stipulated that financial police could carry arms and wear a uniform, and they had the power to act in accordance with the Law On Internal Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was in force at the time. What it meant was that they could bring in those people to the police or whatever it was that this law stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Since this is a new institution, could you please tell us, if you recall, how long it actually took to put this institution in place, in other words, to advertise for the positions, make the selections, do the training so that actually the financial police are able to carry out the functions as envisaged.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it was very difficult to find competent people to do this job and to do it for the HZ HB, because people felt much more comfortable in their municipalities when it came to monitoring and checking the revenues. We appointed the director of the revenues -- revenue department from Ljubuski, one of the municipalities. Before the war he was the director of the revenue department. He had a lot of experience and knowledge. He was a colleague of mine. And when I was a director of one of the revenue departments he was appointed the chief inspector of the revenue department. It was difficult to find people. Some people were mobilised. We had to get them to be demobilised. And we also hired some interns, young people who did not have much experience but who had university degrees, so they went out in the field with their more experienced colleagues. But I think that at the end of 1993 the financial police had 11 employees, not more than that, but it operated throughout the area, and it contributed significantly to the effort to locate and collect revenues for the HZ HB budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe you said it was at the end of 1993, just to make sure that it's accurately reflected in the record, that you had the 11 members of the financial police. We're talking about the end. Okay.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. At the end of the next year. They were established in December 1992, and now we're talking about the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at 1D 02103 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I'm sorry. Before moving on to another document, I'd like to spend a little bit more time discussing this document on the special police. In Article 14 it is stated that the appointments and dismissals are being published in the Official Gazette. We said this was being done for the system to be transparent. But in Article 13, let me translate, the officers of the special police have exceptional powers and are hired without vacancies being posted beforehand. How can one reconcile Article 13 with Article 14, Witness? Why are those vacancies not posted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my document I don't have Article 13. I can't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps you could check the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It perhaps might be of some assistance. It's a bad scan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Yes. That's clear now. In Article 13 it is stipulated that the financial police, the financial police, officials with special powers shall be employed without job vacancies being announced. We felt there was no need for any job vacancies being announced publicly because we knew all the people who met the requirements in HZ HB more or less. We didn't have the time to go through this process because we wanted to be operational as soon as possible, to have the system in place, but to ensure transparency and to make it possible for people to react after their appointment, we published the appointments in the Official Gazette. So you could see from the Official Gazette who was appointed, and then the Presidency of the HZ HB could ask questions if they thought that somebody did not meet the requirements. It had the power to do so. All the more so because the municipal authorities that had representatives in the Presidency of the HVO HZ HB were not happy with the fact that the HVO HZ HB actually passed this kind of a decree, because if you look at Article 47, it says that if an inspector of the financial police of this institution that we're talking about observes any irregularities in the work of the inspectors of the municipal administrations, at the municipal level, the financial police inspector can submit a request to the head of the office in the municipality to launch proceedings for the dismissal of the said inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One small comment of a technical nature. I saw a contradiction between Article 28 and 33. Article 28 states that the inspectors are entitled to carry weapons in the event of four situations. In Article 33, it is stated that the inspector needs to refer to the local police. Is there not a contradiction here, to provide an inspector with weapons and then turn round and say, well, if he needs a problem, he has to turn to the police for help?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says in this Article that if the inspectors -- if the inspector is unable to deal with the situation with his own sidearms. For instance, if he or she faces five armed people, of course then the inspector cannot do anything and then they have to go to the police and the police has to provide protection to the inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told us that there were 11 of them and this was operating until 1993. Was this department efficient? Were you able to highlight violations of customs laws? Unless these were the questions you were about to put, Mr. Karnavas, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There may have been something lost in translation. He indicated that it wasn't operational until 1993. In other words, it began at the end of December 1993 for it to be operational, and the question, at least in English, it appears that from 1992 to 1993 the question is what was able to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this department operated after December 1993. And did you achieve any positive results?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The department became operational in December 1993, and in the first reports there is a column about the revenues obtained through the work of the financial police, and we're talking about substantial amounts. I have to say that the financial police worked until the federal financial police was set up. So that was in 1995, 1996, and at that time the director of the financial police became the deputy director of the federal financial police and the employees, the inspectors, became part of the federal financial police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're speaking of the director. This would have been under the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna because you say in 1995 and you mention a director and it's important for us to understand which director at which period and from where. So the director and the employees, this would have been under -- at that point the director would have been 1994, at least would have been the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna when the financial police began to operate. All right. Let me -- Mr. Tomic, let me ask the question again. There's no need -- the answer's not in the documents. I just want to clarify your answer here, because you said the director and the employees became part of the federal system. Which director are we speaking of?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're speaking of the chief inspector of the financial police, the director of the financial police in the common parlance. The chief inspector of the financial police, he was the chief of the financial police of the HZ HB, and in the next stage of the HR HB, and then when the federal institution was set up he became the deputy director because that was the agreement, that the Muslim should be the director and a Croat his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That's what I wanted to clarify. And the employees who had been working with the financial police that had started under the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, later on the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, they were also employed or continued to be employed in their capacity but now for the federal financial police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next document 1D 02103. This is dated 2 December 1992. We see this is a conclusion, and it relates to export customs documentation. Could you please explain what this is about.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the conclusions that had to assist the strengthening of the financial system and the collection of customs duty and taxes. Up until that time, humanitarian aid was declared -- was cleared through the customs when the truck came to the border crossing, and there was this option that people availed themselves of, and this is why this conclusion was passed, that somebody buys a truck full of underwear to be sold on in HZ HB, but on the arrival at the border crossing this person states to the border control service that this is humanitarian aid and this person then has a piece of paper indicating that it is humanitarian aid. And this conclusion stipulates that once the goods come to the border crossing in HZ HB, it must have regular export documentation originating from the country where the goods were manufactured. If it comes from Croatia, it has to have export declaration from the municipality where the relevant customs office is, for instance, in Zagreb, indicating that this is humanitarian aid. This made is easier for us to distinguish between humanitarian aid and commercial goods, because in the customs offices in Slovenia, Croatia, Germany, wherever the goods originated from, they wanted to get the -- asked for the original documents indicating where the goods were from. So this is not about imposing customs duty on the goods but just on the classification of the goods. They had to be classified as humanitarian aid at the time of their arrival at the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 02744. This is dated 3 December 1992, and here we have an example of a sales contract. If you could explain what is this about. If you just briefly look at it.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a contract about the purchase of salt for -- for the roads in the wintertime. And these goods were bought by the HZ HB at Ceste, which is a public company for road maintenance. And this salt was intended for the maintenance of the Road of Salvation, which at the time was the only link between Herzegovina, Central Bosnia, and Tuzla, and further on to Croatia and other countries. This contract shows that HVO Ceste had bought salt from a company in Tuzla and that delivery is to be made at the service stations of the maintenance company along the road. And the manner of delivery is also stated, and there is also an additional remark that if the buyer wants the seller to transport, to deliver the goods, then the buyer must also pay for the fuel, the reason being that there wasn't enough fuel available for commercial activities. Means of payment with regard to this, you can see that the company from Tuzla, the salt mine, had a non-resident account with Zagrebacka Banka and the payment was to be made to that account, 30 per cent in -- in dinars and the rest as compensation by way of barter. There is also mention of the UNHCR, who they turned to for the maintenance of this road, which was, as I said, the only link between these areas in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that -- for that. Now I want to go step-by-step and go back a little bit. First you indicated that this was a company in Tuzla. Was Tuzla under the ABiH at the time? Was it controlled under the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, looking at the payment method, again just if we go step-by-step, we see that it makes reference to Croatian dinars. So this is a Muslim municipality under ABiH control. It makes reference to Croatian dinars, and also we see a non-residential account. Would this be -- is this account in BiH or is it in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That account was in the Republic of Croatia, and it was opened based on an agreement between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina on non-resident accounts, but this company we're talking about before the war delivered salt for roads throughout Yugoslavia, and they had their warehouses in Croatia, Slovenia, and other republics where in the summertime they would deliver salt which in the wintertime was used for the roads. When war activities started, this company, like others that had similar warehouses opened, a non-resident account under the agreement I mentioned, and the goods they sold off their warehouses in Croatia were paid to those non-resident accounts. And using the money on that account, they purchased goods that they distributed to their employees or to the municipality to survive at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I -- I only mentioned that because we have heard testimony concerning the use of non-residential accounts and whether they were legal or illegal at the time. If we go on to the next item we see now that about -- about 50 per cent is to be paid in what appeared Bosnian dinar, but then there's some reference to the Deutschmark medium rate at the Tuzla bank, Tuzlanska Banka. Could you explain what this is about in a very concrete way?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a contract based on a template, a standard template, and 50 per cent of the price was to be paid in BH dinars to the account stated, but the prices in the contract are in Deutschmarks. And this is about setting the exchange rate, and the exchange rate was that of the Tuzlanska Banka. Through the Zenica branch office of the SDK or another branch office conducting domestic payment transactions the Republic of BiH with the SDK Tuzla branch office, which means that there was no communication between Herzegovina and Tuzla. And they leave open the possibility for payment to be effected in Zenica. So that somebody brings cash and pay it into the account in Zenica, and Zenica will then transfer it to Tuzla, the one SDK branch offers to the other. Which means that there was communication between Tuzla and Zenica. So payment had to be done at a branch office that was connected with Tuzla, be it Zenica or a place around Tuzla. And the exchange rate is the median rate of the Tuzlanska Banka, Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just one question with respect to communications. You said that from Herzegovina to Zenica these communications and from Zenica with Tuzla there are communications. Can you please explain to us why wasn't it possible to have direct communications from Herzegovina all the way to Tuzla, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we spoke about that yesterday. Telecommunications had been disrupted and could not be used. We couldn't transfer the monies in the usual way. Zenica is -- was mentioned as the chief branch office that is closest to Herzegovina. Even Zenica and Tuzla were not in direct communication. There were payment orders brought in written form or carried in written form from Zenica to Tuzla. They had to go over a mountain. And then Zenica would -- would effect payment based on those orders on behalf of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Zenica was under the control of the ABiH. Was it not?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me take this example of a company selling salt, which was in an ABiH-controlled area. We're now talking about 1992, 1993. Back then did the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina export abroad, for instance to Croatia? Were they companies that kept exporting manufactured goods, goods that were manufactured in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were companies which sold such goods throughout that time, goods that they had in their warehouses and that were produced in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
